articles.title: Nothing Headphone 1 review: head-turning
articles.summary: At $299, the Nothing Headphone 1 aims to take on more expensive flagship Bluetooth headphones from Bose, Sony, and Apple.
articles.body: Nothing’s first pair of over-the-ear headphones has arrived, bearing the company’s signature retro-transparent design that it introduced with the Phone 1. But until now, that design has mostly been in your pocket or peeking out of your ears. With the $299 Nothing Headphone 1, you have to commit to having that aesthetic wrapped around your head or hanging from your neck. I spent about a week with the Headphone 1 to see how it fits among the competition — and with your outfit. [Product: Nothing Headphone 1 | The Nothing Headphone 1 resembles a cross between Apple’s AirPods Max and 1980s FM radio headphones. I dig the design, but wearing it on my head feels silly. The housing feels cheaper than the aluminum casing of the $549 AirPods Max and also less… grown up. I’m almost embarrassed to wear it on the street and worried that I’ll look like I’m cosplaying as a cyborg. The ear pads look like that of generic headphones, with rubbery and plastic unremovable pads and a memory foam center. Though I don’t care for the texture, they’re comfortable, and I haven’t felt fatigued while wearing them throughout the day like I do with the Sony WH-1000XM6. [Image: [Image: The button design is my favorite part of the headphones. The volume is controlled by the roller, which is like a rubbery wheel you spin, not too far off from Apple’s digital crown, but oriented on its side. Pressing on the roller plays or pauses your audio, and holding it down toggles one of three modes — noise canceling, transparency, or off. There’s also the paddle button, allowing you to skip tracks, go backward to previous tracks, fast forward or rewind, or hang up or decline phone calls when held down. I have yet to find an app that works with the fast forward / rewind control, but Nothing claims this is dependent on the platform. A customizable button on the outside of the right ear cup can be set to launch a voice assistant like Google Gemini, use an EQ preset, mute the microphone, control noise, or enable spatial audio. These customizations are done with the Nothing X app (available on iOS and Android). If you use the Headphone 1 with the Nothing Phone 3, you can use that button to “channel hop” between different audio apps — a feature that will eventually be rolled out to other Nothing devices. I wasn’t able to test this, since I don’t have a Phone 3. [Image: It looks very cool when not on my head. The Headphone 1 features head tracking, allowing you to anchor your position while listening to audio and rotate the panning according to how you turn your head. This is a trend among flagship headphones — like Apple’s spatial audio, Bose’s immersive mode, and Sony’s spatial audio mixing — but it’s not something I ever want to use. It does not sound very believable, and most of the time, it makes the audio sound worse. Much like the worst versions of Apple Music’s spatial audio tracks, it emulates that “stadium” mode from old stereo receivers. Noise canceling works well, outside of calls. It’s a little easier to deliver good active noise cancellation (ANC) with over-the-ear headphones than with earbuds because of their size and ability to cover your entire ear, but I’ve found the Nothing headphones can block subway sounds, loud hums, and other city din with ease. I would feel comfortable bringing these as my travel headphones on a trip. I won’t get over-analytical with the sound quality, but nothing stands out as bad compared to other flagship headphones. I don’t think the Headphone 1 sounds as good as the AirPods Max, but I prefer Nothing’s frequency response to Bose’s QuietComfort Ultra and Sony’s WH-1000XM6. This is on par with Nothing’s earbuds line and even its budget CMF-branded earpieces, which compete surprisingly well with other flagship earbuds. Nothing says the Headphone 1 has “four built-in microphones with AI-powered Clear Voice Technology to isolate your speech and suppress background noise.” It certainly suppresses a ton of background noise, and even in a train station, I was able to take a call with the participants hearing my voice pretty clearly. At least they could once I put the headphones on the right way around. There is a design issue with the Nothing Headphone 1: unlike the AirPods Max, when you fold them flat to put them into the case, the left ear is on the right side, and the right on the left. So unless you flip them around when you pick them up out of the case — a very awkward move — you’re going to put them on backwards, as I did the first time I tried the voice call experiment. When you do wear them correctly, though, the audio is easily understandable and takes out almost any other noise completely. The headphones also do not seem to have multipoint; Nothing responded by saying there is dual connection on the headphones, but I am not easily able to switch between devices without going into the device’s settings each time. [Image: [Image: [Image: The Headphone 1 comes in a slim, softshell zipper case that’s made of a material prone to picking up the fur of my white cat. The zipper is a little finicky and gets caught easily when closing, but it seals pretty well when fully zipped. [Image: I appreciate the pouch for the cables. It’s also very easy to understand how they fit in the case, as long as you remember the red square is on the right ear cup. The Headphone 1 also comes with a Nothing-designed USB-C cable, which can be used for both charging and listening, and a 3.5mm cable for listening on analog headphone jacks. The analog jack doesn’t work when the headphones are off or when charging, so if the battery dies, they’re unusable until you find a USB port. That’s unfortunate, especially if / when these batteries die of old age. But you can listen over Bluetooth or USB-C while recharging, at least. Nothing promises up to 35 hours of battery life with ANC on and using the AAC codec (probably the most common scenario) and 37 hours of talk time with just ANC on. With ANC off, Nothing claims the headphones offer up to 80 hours of playback using the AAC codec and 54 hours with the LDAC codec. After a week of casual use and using them throughout my workday, I never had to charge them, and I had gone two days without plugging them in. The $299 Nothing Headphone 1 offers many features that compete well with Bose, Apple, and Sony, and the lower price might get some folks to choose it. If the design fits your personality, then saving $200 for this audio quality and noise cancellation makes this a package worth considering. Correction, July 2nd: In our initial tests, we incorrectly assessed the headphones’ mic quality due to having the headphones on backwards during one portion of our testing. We’ve rerun our tests and updated the review to reflect the (obviously) improved mic results and to discuss our concern with the way the headphones fold flat for storage. Photography by Owen Grove / The Verge

articles.title: Upcoming New Star Wars Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond
articles.summary: What do Star Wars fans have to look forward to next? A whole lot, as it turns out. From TV series like Ahsoka Season 2 to the Ryan Gosling Starfighter movie, here are all the Star Wars projects in the works right now (and a few that have stalled out).
articles.body:
The first Star Wars movie in seven years, The Mandalorian and Grogu, finally arrived in 2026, for better or worse, but there are still a bunch of other big Star Wars projects in the works, like Ahsoka: Season 2 , a new Star Wars movie starring Ryan Gosling called Starfighter which is being directed by Deadpool & Wolverine's Shawn Levy, and more. And yet amid all that, Kathleen Kennedy, president of Lucasfilm, has stepped down from her duties, with long-time Star Wars creator Dave Filoni and Lynwen Brennan replacing her. Filoni now serves as President and Chief Creative Officer while Brennan is Co-President.

While Kennedy's departure had been rumored for some time, now that it actully happened it's clear that the Star Wars franchise is at a critical juncture. Will Filoni and Brennan be able to revive excitement in fans and mainstream audiences about what has been seen as something of a lagging series in recent years?

So let's take a look at all of the upcoming Star Wars movies and TV shows that we know about. While some are locked, others on our list are just industry reports that haven't been confirmed by Disney yet. We've also kept some older projects on our list that have long since been snuffed out, like the Jedi themselves! Their fire has gone out of the universe...

Click right through the scruffy-looking slideshow below to see what's coming, and a couple of "maybes" too...

What Are the Next Star Wars Movies and TV Shows Coming Out? 2026 Release Dates

For those keeping track, here's the full lineup of upcoming Star Wars movies and TV shows:

Dave Filoni's Mando-Verse/New Republic Movie

Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy's New Jedi Order/Rey Movie

The Mandalorian: Season 4 / The Book of Boba Fett: Season 2

Star Wars: Rangers of the New Republic Series

David Benioff & DB Weiss' Star Wars Movies

Here are the Star Wars projects that are closest to becoming a reality (or at least were in recent times)...

The next Star Wars movie hitting theaters after The Mandalorian and Grogu is Star Wars: Starfighter , directed by Deadpool & Wolverine's Shawn Levy and starring the Driver himself, Ryan Gosling. The film is set roughly five years after the events of The Rise of Skywalker, putting it further down the Star Wars timeline than any movie or show to date.

Levy has been developing the project with scripter Jonathan Tropper since 2022. Tropper previously worked with the director on This Is Where I Leave You and The Adam Project. According to The Hollywood Reporter , the movie will be unrelated to the Skywalker Saga and will be a standalone story.

When Ahsoka: Season 1 ended on a cliffhanger, it was unclear whether those loose ends would be picked up in a second season or feed directly into Dave Filoni's Mando-verse movie. But production has now wrapped on Ahsoka: Season 2 and the series is set to return at the beginning of January.

The Star Wars franchise remained in the post-Clone Wars, pre-A New Hope era for this animated series, which focuses on the former Darth Maul as he seeks to rebuild his criminal empire in the age of the Empire. Sam Witwer reprises his role as Maul. We gave Season 1 an 8 out of 10, and a second season is already in the works.

Dave Filoni's Mando-Verse/New Republic Movie (In Development)

Dave Filoni will make the jump from Star Wars shows to the big screen. Filoni is directing a movie set after the events of Return of the Jedi. The film is said to tie together shows like The Mandalorian, The Book of Boba Fett and Ahsoka.

Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy's New Jedi Order Movie (In Development)

Ms. Marvel's Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy is directing the first Star Wars film set after the events of The Rise of Skywalker. Daisy Ridley will return to reprise the role of Rey Skywalker, with the film focusing on Rey's efforts to rebuild the Jedi after the final battle with Emperor Palpatine. It's expected that other actors from the Sequel Trilogy will also return.

At various points in its development, Damon Lindelof and Justin Britt-Gibson, and then Steven Knight, were attached to write the film. However, all have since left the project. Reports previously indicated that Rey as a character was still a major priority at Disney, and in January, 2025, George Nolfi (The Bourne Ultimatum) was the latest writer hired to script the film. But when Kathleen Kennedy announced her resignation from Lucasfilm in January, 2026, she did not mention the Rey project while discussing other films in development. Huh.

Simon Kinberg's Star Wars Trilogy (In Development)

In 2024 news broke that X-Men producer (and Star Wars Rebels co-creator) Simon Kinberg had been tapped to oversee a brand-new trilogy of Star Wars films . Kinberg will write the trilogy and produce. Sources gave conflicting reports as to what the trilogy will actually be about, though. It may be a direct continuation of the Skywalker Saga, effectively making Kinberg the architect of Episodes X through XII. However, others claimed the trilogy will focus on a new storyline. In January, 2026, Kathleen Kennedy revealed that Kinberg wrote something that was "very good, but not there. We’ve pretty much upended the story, and then spent a great deal of time on the treatment." From there she said Kinberg was expected to turn in "something" -- presumably a screenplay -- by March, 2026. All of which is to say it's still early days on this one.

Taika Waititi's Star Wars Movie (On Hold or Status Unknown)

Thor: Ragnarok's Taika Waititi was tapped to direct a live-action Star Wars movie at one point, which he would co-write with 1917's Krysty Wilson-Cairns. Nothing else is known about the film yet, including when it's set in the Star Wars timeline... or if it will even happen. Kathleen Kennedy said in January, 2026, that she thinks the project is "still somewhat alive." Hope springs eternal!

The film dates back to at least 2021, when Waititi revealed he'd cracked the story for his movie , but the actual script was still in its early stages. In May, 2022, Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said that this would be the next Star Wars film released, while in March, 2023, Variety reported that it could be the project that snaps up the then-empty December, 2025, release date on Lucasfilm's slate. In February, 2025, however, Kennedy confirmed that she still hasn't seen a finished script from Waititi , saying “if we ever do get a script from Taika, it’s going to be fantastic.”

James Mangold's Dawn of the Jedi Movie (On Hold or Status Unknown)

At Star Wars Celebration 2023, we learned that Logan director James Mangold was going to be directing a movie about the very first Jedi Knights. Little was known about the movie, other than that it would be set roughly 25,000 years before the other films and would be "biblical" in scope. Unfortunately, in January, 2026, Kathleen Kennedy said that the film is now on the "back burner."

Star Wars: Lando Movie (On Hold or Status Unknown)

While Lucasfilm seems to have no plans for a sequel to 2018's Solo: A Star Wars Story, Donald Glover's Lando Calrissian was supposed to get his own live-action series at one point. The project was announced in December 2020, and was being developed by Dear White People's Justin Simien. However, Simien eventually departed the project, with Glover and his brother Stephen Glover taking over as writers. And in the fall of 2023 Stephen revealed that Lando was expected to take shape as a movie rather than a show. As of January, 2026, Kathleen Kennedy said that the project was "still somewhat alive." Great!

The Mandalorian: Season 4 / The Book of Boba Fett: Season 2 (On Hold or Status Unknown)

There's currently no word on a fourth season of The Mandalorian or a second season of The Book of Boba Fett. The box office performance of The Mandalorian and Grogu may mean the former series has ended its small-screen run, and we're not holding our breath for more The Book of Boba Fett at this point.

Carlton & Nick Cuse's Star Wars Series (On Hold or Status Unknown)

Lost co-showrunner Carlton Cuse was developing a streaming Star Wars series with his son, Watchmen and The Leftovers writer Nick Cuse, at one point. That's virtually all we know about this mysterious project, as there's no word on the plot, timeline, characters, or other story details yet. And with Disney seemingly pulling back on greenlighting new Star Wars streaming shows now, it seems unlikely that this one will move forward any time soon.

The Hunt for Ben Solo Movie (Canceled/Dead)

Fans got very excited when word came that Adam Driver and filmmaker Steven Soderbergh had pitched a Hunt for Ben Solo movie , even though the project was not given the go-ahead. A fan campaign since then has not led Disney or Lucasfilm to reverse their decision, but Kathleen Kennedy has said that “Steve Soderbergh and Adam Driver turned in a script written by Scott Burns ... It was just great. Anything’s a possibility if somebody’s willing to take a risk.” Alas, it seems Soderbergh and Driver have moved on.

Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (Canceled/Dead)

Wonder Woman director Patty Jenkins was given the reins of a Star Wars theatrical film, which was originally slated to hit theaters in Christmas of 2023. Kathleen Kennedy teased, "This story will introduce a new generation of starfighter pilots as they earn their wings and risk their lives in a boundary-pushing, high-speed thrill ride. The legend of Rogue Squadron has been long beloved by Star Wars fans, and will move us into a future era of the galaxy."

However, as of November 2021 the film was no longer on the production schedule while Jenkins reportedly focused on Wonder Woman 3 (which has since been cancelled). Industry insider Matthew Belloni reported the film was the latest in a long line of Star Wars projects hampered by "creative differences." And in March of 2023, Variety reported that a source has stated that the film is no longer in active development. In April of that year, Kennedy told IGN the following: "Rogue Squadron, that definitely is something that we still talk about. Whether it's a movie, or whether it ends up being in the series space, that's definitely something." Of course, Kennedy is no longer with the company so...

Note: This story was updated on 9/9/2026. It was originally posted on 7/29/2021.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on Twitter .

articles.title: The Razr Fold is stuck in the middle
articles.summary: The Motorola Razr Fold comes with excellent battery life and thoughtful styling, but it’s a little too unremarkable for its $1,900 price.
articles.body: For a phone that gets a lot right, the Motorola Razr Fold is frustratingly hard to recommend. The Razr Fold is the company’s first book-style foldable, and it enters the US market with something not currently available on the competition: truly excellent battery life that rivals the best slab-style phones. No need to worry if you spend a long session gaming or working in a Google doc on the inner screen. The Razr Fold is going to easily get you through your day and then some. Samsung’s and Google’s foldables are much more likely to generate battery anxiety on a day of heavy use. Also, the Razr Fold looks nice. The rounded corners, soft-touch back panel, and well-considered color options are very welcome and very Motorola. Nobody is making better-looking phones than this company right now. As a reminder, it’s okay to care about how your phone looks. But the Razr Fold sets a very high bar for itself by virtue of costing $1,900. And at that price, it falls short in a few ways. This is a phone that puts all of its polish front and center — a great design, a big battery, and a clever multitasking system — but then drops the act around the edges. And there are a few too many rough edges for this high-end of a device. [Product: Motorola Razr Fold | The Razr Fold’s 6,000mAh battery really is its biggest asset. It’s able to offer so much capacity thanks to its silicon-carbon technology, allowing it to store more energy than traditional lithium-ion batteries. Chinese phone makers are quickly adopting it while Apple, Samsung, and Google have been reluctant — likely because of some concerns about the battery tech degrading faster than straight-up lithium-ion. Motorola and its China-based parent company Lenovo seem not to share the same concerns, since this year’s entire Razr lineup uses silicon-carbon tech. It’s hard to say how justified the concerns are around longevity since silicon-carbon hasn’t been used in phones for that long. In my extremely unscientific opinion and limited short-term testing, I can say that silicon-carbon absolutely kicks ass in a phone. I never even came close to triggering low power mode on the Razr Fold. Even on a day with a healthy amount of camera use and an hour using the inner screen, the battery was still above 50 percent by bedtime. Motorola has also figured out a multitasking solution on the inner screen that rivals could learn from. It feels like a good compromise between Samsung’s “anything goes” approach and Google’s three app maximum. You can open two apps in split-screen or have one app occupy most of the screen with a second in the background just a quick tap away. On top of that, you can embrace chaos and open multiple apps in small “freeform” windows you can resize and move around the screen. I got up to four apps running in this mode on top of two apps operating in split-screen before I decided it was too much stimulation. But I like this meet-in-the-middle approach that allows me to invite as much or as little chaos as I want. [Image: I’m not saying you should run four apps at once, but I’m not not saying it. Battery and multitasking are pretty important things to get right on a folding phone. And yet, the Razr Fold disappoints in other ways. For starters, there are entirely too many preloaded apps on a device of this stature. Many, but not all of them, can be uninstalled. But just on principle, I don’t think anyone should have to spend time clearing out bloatware on a phone that costs this much. The Fold is also missing some small but life-improving hardware upgrades. There are no Qi2 magnets built into the back of the phone, and I increasingly believe every phone should have magnets. The Fold supports wireless charging, but you won’t be able to thwack it onto a MagSafe-style charger like you can with the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. And while I appreciate Motorola making a stylus for the Razr Fold, there’s no way to attach it to the phone and no case for the Fold with a place to store it. I forgot to bring it with me on more than one trip to a coffee shop where I intended to use it. The stylus is sold separately for $99 anyway, so maybe it’s a fair assumption that if you’re going out of the way to get one, you’re committed enough to figuring out the carry situation on your own. [Image: Two phones for the price of two phones. Aside from the silicon-carbon battery, the Razr Fold doesn’t break any new ground hardware-wise. It’s less heavy and bulky than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, but lacks that phone’s full dust resistance. And although the Razr Fold is leaner than the Pixel, it still constantly reminds me that I’m carrying it when it’s in my bag or pocket. The Z Fold 7, which costs $100 more than the Razr Fold, is appreciably smaller and lighter. That’s its whole deal. The Fold is kind of in no-man’s land between the incumbents, and that’s an uncomfortable place to be if you’re going to charge a premium. Recent Motorola phones have been pretty weak in the camera department — forgivable on a $400 phone but not one that costs $1,900. There’s some good news: Image processing looks better on the Razr Fold than it has on past Motorola phones. I see less tendency toward overly bright, washed-out images. Photos in bright daylight show pleasant contrast and saturated blues. The 50-megapixel ultrawide is a cut above the usual 12-megapixel chip, producing plenty of sharp detail. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Consistency is the thing, though, and the Razr Fold’s camera system occasionally missteps. I noticed a jarring change in color cast a couple of times when switching between the wide and telephoto. The tendency to boost shadows too aggressively also shows up here and there, particularly when I’m using the 2x crop zoom, or photographing a gray, overcast scene outdoors. I’m also not a fan of the generative AI-augmented digital zoom that kicks in above 20x. It introduces some artifacts when trying to clean up text — classic AI. There’s also an uncanniness to the way it processes small details in a scene, like distant features in the side of a building. They look too clean, and features are sort of smoothed out and blended in a way that just looks unnatural. Thankfully, there’s some text that pops up on the screen when it kicks in, and you can turn the feature totally off in settings. [Image: Tent mode is still a pretty neat trick. If Motorola had launched the Razr Fold four years ago, I might feel differently about it. The Galaxy Z Fold was still growing out of its awkward too-tall shape, and the Pixel Fold didn’t exist at all yet. A folding phone with sophisticated styling? With a battery that lasts all day? That might have been worth $1,900 back then, considering there was nothing like that at the time. But it’s 2026, which is an unfortunate time to be launching a pricey phone. The memory crisis surely played a part in the Razr Fold’s high price. Samsung and Google will likely launch successors to their folding phones later this summer, and I won’t be surprised if their prices go up. But here and now, the Razr Fold feels like a bit too little, for too much, too late. Photography by Allison Johnson / The Verge --- Agree to continue: Motorola Razr Fold Every smart device now requires you to agree to a series of terms and conditions before you can use it — contracts that no one actually reads. It’s impossible for us to read and analyze every single one of these agreements. But we started counting exactly how many times you have to hit “agree” to use devices when we review them since these are agreements most people don’t read and definitely can’t negotiate. To actually use the Motorola Razr Fold, you must accept the following: * Motorola’s Privacy and Software Updates But you also get to decide how Motorola’s support works on your phone: * Help improve Motorola products (optional) * Enhanced device support (optional) * Smart updates (optional) After entering your Google account, you are asked to: * Add a phone number to your Google account (optional) And you must agree to the following from Google: * Google Terms of Service * Google Privacy Policy * Google Play Terms of Service You’ll also need to agree to the following on Google Services: * Install updates and apps: “You agree this device may also automatically download and install updates and apps from Google, your carrier, and your device’s manufacturer, possibly using cellular data. Some of these apps may offer in-app purchases.” * Use basic device backup (optional) * Use location (optional) * Allow scanning (optional) * Send usage and diagnostic data (optional) Google Assistant: * You can set up Google Assistant (optional) * Activate Voice Match for Hey Google (optional) * Access Assistant without unlocking your device (optional) To use Moto AI: * Motorola AI Terms and Conditions (optional) Lastly, you have the option to join Motorola’s user community: * Give permission to Motorola to send push notifications about its services and benefits (optional) * Provide your email to Motorola (optional) In total, you have to accept five main agreements and can bypass 14 when setting up the Motorola Razr Fold.

articles.title: Qi fan fan
articles.summary: Active cooling really works as demonstrated on a Kuxiu D5  Qi2.2 charging dock. Useful at Qi 25W, it’ll likely be required for QI 50W.
articles.body: Despite my initial skepticism, I’m now sold on wireless Qi chargers that add integrated fans to keep your phone cool while charging. I figured they’d be too loud, or too weak, or too gimmicky, but I’m a convert after spending a week with the new $59.99 Kuxiu D5 Qi2.2 charging dock. Its active cooling system has kept my phone from heating up, unlike every other Qi charger I’ve tried. Good thing, given my own history with an overheating phone. Last year I fried the logic board on my titanium iPhone 15 Pro. I was on a sweltering train and trying to edit a 4K video on my phone, which was charging from a magnetically attached Qi power bank. Oof, my iPhone is getting really hot, I thought, just as the screen went forever blank. The repair bill was €660.33 (over $750), for which I paid nothing because it was just inside the two-year warranty. Apple’s “genius” wouldn’t say if the phone overheated, but I’m not keen to tempt fate twice. Heat is the enemy of batteries. High temperatures accelerate the chemical degradation of lithium-ion cells, permanently reducing how much charge they can hold over time. The electromagnetic induction employed by Qi chargers is inherently inefficient, producing far more heat than transferring electricity through a cable plugged into your phone. That heat can cause phones to throttle the wireless charging speed in order to protect the battery. Despite knowing this, I keep coming back to Qi charging docks and power banks because they’re so damn convenient. I’m also addicted to Apple’s StandBy feature that turns my phone into a desk or bedside clock and widget machine when docked and charging in landscape orientation. Fortunately, companies like Anker, Aukey, ESR, and Kuxiu have started building active cooling systems directly into their Qi chargers. They feature tiny heat sinks and ultra-quiet internal fans that actively blow the heat away from the back of your phone while it charges. This keeps the battery significantly cooler and allows for faster charging speeds. Powerful magnets ensure perfect alignment between the phone’s receiver coil and the charger’s transmitter coil to maximize efficiency and minimize heat waste. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The fan inside the Kuxiu D5 operates silently, but it can still be turned off if you want. The display is useful, but the little winky-faced screensaver is not. I do like knowing the time and how much charge each device is pulling, in addition to the total power draw, but the animated movement is distracting when caught out of the corner of my eye. It’s also a bit too bright for my taste when perched on my nightstand. Fortunately, I can turn the display off with a tap of a button. I like that the Kuxiu D5 ships with a 45W USB-C PD charger in the box. Otherwise, you’d have to guess if whatever charger you have lying around will support the dock’s max total output, which can deliver up to 25W to Qi2.2-compatible phones, 2.5W to Qi-compatible watches, and 5W to Qi-compatible earbuds. It’s compatible with several generations of phones, watches, and earbuds sold by Apple, Samsung, and others. Kuxiu calls the D5 a “5-in-1” charger, which I find misleading since it’ll only charge up to three devices simultaneously. It seems to include the display and fan in its total. By that count, I’d be happier if this was a 4-in-1 device, since the added cost for the display won’t add much value for most people, and it can only cause issues down the road. The watch charger is also a little silly in its over-engineering. A long-press on the dock’s sole button kicks off a tiny motor to slowly push the watch dock out the side. I guess it adds to the blocky dock’s durability when traveling, but not by much, and it can only be retracted when the dock is plugged into the wall. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Overall the Kuxiu D5 is a fine Qi2.2 charging dock made better by active cooling. It’s equally at home on a desktop or nightstand, and priced below similar docks from Anker, ESR, and others. Active cooling on Qi chargers is a good idea whose time has come. Phones sold by Huawei, Xiaomi, and Oppo have supported wireless charging speeds of 50W and above for years. But that’s only possible when placed on proprietary charging docks capable of whisking away all the extra waste heat. Now the body responsible for Qi is working on a global 50W standard for release by 2028. Manufacturers will likely need to adopt active cooling to reliably sustain those higher charging rates. Fine by me. Whatever it takes to keep that vital Qi life force flowing. All photography by Thomas Ricker / The Verge

articles.title: EA is now a private company
articles.summary: Electronic Arts has officially become a private company. An investor group led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners has taken the company private.
articles.body: Electronic Arts has officially become a private company. Last September, EA announced that an investor group led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners would be taking the company private in a $55 billion deal, and on Tuesday, EA said the deal successfully closed. The PIF will reportedly own 93.4 percent of the new company. The deal includes $20 billion of debt financing — making it the largest leveraged buyout ever — which could mean big changes at EA to justify the deal. As of late, EA has been focusing heavily on its big tentpole franchises, including things like Battlefield, its sports games like EA Sports FC and Madden NFL, and The Sims. Given the stakes of the deal, it seems likely that EA will depend more on bankable releases rather than experimenting on smaller games — a strategy that many of the industry’s biggest publishers, including Ubisoft and Xbox, are shifting toward as well. ”As we begin this next chapter, I’m more optimistic than ever about what we’ll create together,” CEO Andrew Wilson said in a message to staff. “The opportunities ahead are extraordinary, and they’ll be brought to life by our creativity, our ambition, and our belief in what’s possible.” The deal for EA follows other major video game industry acquisitions in recent years, including Microsoft’s $68.7 billion deal for Activision Blizzard, its $7.5 billion deal for Bethesda Softworks parent company ZeniMax Media, and Take-Two’s $12.7 billion deal for Zynga.

articles.title: Redwall's 23rd and Final Book Is Finally Getting Published After 16 Years
articles.summary: The 23rd and final novel in Brian Jacques’ Redwall series will be published in September 2027, putting an end to the beloved saga after 41 years.
articles.body:
The 23rd and final novel in Brian Jacques’ Redwall series will be published in September 2027, putting an end to the beloved saga after 41 years.

The late, great Jacques still has one more ace up his sleeve. Orphans of Mossflower, the very last Redwall book penned by the celebrated British author, will be released posthumously alongside the saga’s first-ever box set next year.

As spotted by a post on the official Redwall fan Wiki , the digital publishing catalog platform Edelweiss features a frontlist of forthcoming Redwall books, which includes Orphans of Mossflower. As told by the frontlist, this will be the “final book in the series.”

Screens - Lost Legends of Redwall -- The Scout: Act 1

Nothing else about the title was shared, but it’s expected to be a direct sequel to the series’ most recent book, The Rogue Crew — which was published in 2011, a whopping 15 years ago.

Jacques died that same year at 71 after suffering a heart attack. The Rogue Crew was the only Redwall book to be published after his death, meaning that Orphans of Mossflower will be the second. It’s unclear if any additions were made to the novel by his editors, or how far along it was at the time of his death — but we suspect we’ll learn the answers to these questions when it gets closer to being released next year.

For now, theories abound as to what adventures Mossflower's creatures will get up to in this last novel. One hypothesis points to the winner of a 2010 contest who got to create a character that would appear in a future Redwall novel. This character was initially suspected to be in The Rogue Crew, but that didn’t happen — and given that Jacques died shortly before it was published, fans are of the mind that this character might pop up in Orphans of Mossflower.

Speaking to those at the Redwall Wiki, the winner — named Olivia — said she created a haremaiden named Reisa Kartwell, explaining that "’Reisa’ comes from ‘reise,’ meaning ‘travel’ in German, and ‘Kartwell’ is derived from ‘karte,’ the German word for ‘map.’ Reisa is Salamandastron's cartographer, and her map depicting efficient travel paths proves invaluable when the Redwallers must quickly reach Salamandastron when Redwall is under attack.”

The Rogue Crew follows Abbot Thibb, the Longpatrol hares, and the titular rogue crew of sea otters as they defend Redwall Abbey from the vicious Razzid Wearat, who wreaks havoc on his wheeled ship that can traverse both land and sea. We’ll have to see where this story picks up in the final book when it’s published a year from now.

This news follows the sad cancellation of Netflix’s Redwall series earlier this year. Fans of animal-fantasy literature need not worry, though; Erin Hunter’s Warriors book saga is getting a long-awaited animated series on Disney+, as well as a video game , the latter of which will release in October 2026.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

Jimmy Tatro has been cast as Gorilla Grodd, but the actor recently explained that his role is mostly voice work and that motion-capture will be used to record his facial expressions.

That would explain why there’s a performer in a gorilla costume in the set photos and videos all over social media while the production films at Georgia Institute of Technology. It’s likely the suit performer is a stand-in for what will eventually become a CGI character.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid Spiritual Successor Physint Will Now Be Published by Xbox Instead of Sony
articles.summary: Renowned video game director Hideo Kojima's upcoming project Physint, which could fairly be described as a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, will now be published by Xbox instead of Sony, Microsoft announced today. Xbox will continue to publish the horror game OD – itself something of a spiritual successor to the never-finished PT – and the Kojima-Xbox partnership will expand beyond these two game projects to include film and television.
articles.body:
Renowned video game director Hideo Kojima's upcoming project Physint, which could fairly be described as a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, will now be published by Xbox instead of Sony, Microsoft announced today.

Xbox will continue to publish Kojima's horror game OD — itself something of a spiritual successor to the never-finished PT — and the Kojima-Xbox partnership will expand beyond these two game projects to include film and television.

“This expands our relationship with Xbox beyond OD. As we move forward with the development of Physint, we remain committed to redefining the action-espionage genre for players around the world,” Kojima said.

He also posted on X with details on how the deal came to be, saying that Sony was going to cancel Physint. "As confirmed earlier through our official channels, in mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the Physint project. Physint is an important project both to me personally and to Kojima Productions. Determined to keep the project alive, we have spent the last three months searching tirelessly for a new partner. In the course of seeking advice and pursuing negotiations with people across many fields, we found in Xbox a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future, and we have decided to team up with them once again. Please rest assured that development of Physint, our genre-defining action-espionage title, is ongoing and will continue moving forward."

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who took over from the retiring Phil Spencer earlier this year, made Kojima a priority in her quest to reset and rebuild Xbox, including the return of console exclusives that begins with Gears of War: E-Day this year and continues with Clockwork Revolution in 2027 . In terms of Kojima Productions projects, OD will be released before Physint. In July, IGN reported that OD was safe from Sharma's big "reset" of the Xbox business , which has seen thousands of staff lose their jobs, multiple studios go independent, and various video game projects canceled.

“Creators have choices about where and how they bring their ideas to life," Sharma said. "We’re honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on Physint. His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox.” PlayStation issued a statement as well, posting, "After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to step away from collaborating with KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS on its project PHYSINT. We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima's vision for the game. Our relationship remains strong after three decades of industry-leading, genre-defining creative cooperation, and we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future."

When Physint was announced it was heavily backed by Sony. During the 2024 State of Play broadcast, PlayStation Studios boss Hermen Hulst shook Kojima's hand while saying: "Today, I'm excited to announce that together, as part of the PlayStation and Kojima Productions partnership, Hideo's going to take us on an exciting new adventure, one that I've been encouraging him to reinvent for years." Hulst continued: "We're are all really excited about this project, and we weill fully support you with the latest innovations Sony has to offer. More details to come."

Kojima and Hulst ended the announcement by walking off set, the camera pulling away out of the building to reveal a Columbia Pictures sign with the word 'Physint' below it. (Columbia Pictures is owned by the Sony Group Corporation through its subsidiary, Sony Pictures Entertainment.)

The switch from PlayStation to Xbox is a major PR win for Microsoft, which has effectively stolen a Kojima project away from Sony. The last time one first-party platform lost out to another on this kind of AAA level — and the only one I can think of — is when Final Fantasy jumped ship from Nintendo to PlayStation back in the PS1 era.

Physint is a working title, and we still don't know much about it. "Of course, it is an interactive game," Kojima said when Physint was announced, "but it is also a movie at the same time." He continued: "It is a completely new 'Action Espionage' for the next-generation. It will be created using cutting-edge technology and the best talents from around the world, both from film and video games. Of course this is an interactive 'game,' but the look, story, theme, cast, acting, fashion, sound, etc... are all at the next level of 'Digital Entertainment' that could be called a 'movie.'"

It may be some time before Physint comes out, as Kojima said last year that Physint was likely another 5-6 years away . But work on the game is ramping up. Just this week, many fans were left convinced that Batman actor Robert Pattinson will star in the game.

Kojima last officially discussed Physint in September 2025, during a Kojima Productions 10th Anniversary event in Japan . Speaking on-stage during the event, Kojima said development on Physint was just starting, and that he was working on concepts by himself, making characters, and thinking about casting. The tech underpinning Physint was described as even more advanced than that powering Kojima’s Death Stranding games and OD ( whose debut trailer was revealed at the show ).

Kojima did tease the main character of the game via the first poster for Physint, below.

Kojima also confirmed three actors set to appear in Physint, each of whom delivered a video message expressing their excitement. Charlee Fraser, who played Mary Jabassa in Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga , is in the game, although we don’t know which character she’s playing. Also in the game are Don Lee, who played Gilgamesh in the Marvel movie Eternals , and Japanese actress Minami Hamabe, who played Noriko Ōishi in Godzilla Minus One .

Kojima ended his Physint segment with a shot of Hamabe in CG form, showing off just how realistic the visuals are expected to be. We still don't know which game engine Kojima Productions is using for Physint.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Proof-of-Age Verification for Steam in Australia Now Only Possible Using a Credit Card
articles.summary: Unlike PlayStation and Xbox, which offer multiple ways to verify you’re over 18, Valve will only accept ownership of an actual credit card, despite the fact only about half of Australian consumers actually have one.
articles.body:
Valve has implemented a proof-of-age verification system for Australian Steam users, which was required due to new laws in the country forcing online gaming platforms to require users to prove they are over 18 years of age to access games classified R18+. That law actually came into effect way back in March.

However, unlike PlayStation and Xbox (which offer multiple ways to verify you’re over 18), Valve has opted that it will only accept ownership of an actual credit card as sufficient proof of age. Despite some users anecdotally reporting otherwise, it does not appear debit cards are sufficient, and nor is PayPal. It also doesn’t matter if your Steam account is already well over 20 years old.

Without verification, Australian Steam users trying to access the store page of a game rated R18+ will be met by the following message:

“Valve is required by the Age-Restricted Material App Distribution Services Code to verify that you are 18 or older before accessing mature content. If you wish to do so, please add a valid Australian credit card to your account and afterwards update the Mature Content Preferences.”

Of course, not all Australian Steam users over 18 have a credit card, or indeed want a credit card – when there are already a ton of more convenient ways to make purchases online. Unfortunately for Australian Steam users, an active credit card is all Valve is willing to accept, despite other methods of verification being readily available. This active credit card also reportedly needs to remain active on the account, even if you do not want to make purchases with it.

The fact that Valve’s proof-of-age verification “system” has come so late and yet is so unfit for purpose is either arrogance or naivety on the company’s part, considering how significantly credit card ownership in Australia has fallen over the past decade. Today, only around half of Australian consumers even have a credit card, with adoption lowest amongst young adults (only around a quarter of Australian consumers aged 18 to 24 have a credit card). Credit cards are entirely unnecessary to make online purchases in 2026, and Valve should have known better considering its payment option data in Australia ought to have made that more than evident.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

articles.title: In The Wandering Earth: The Last Full Moon, You Must Get Rid of The Moon
articles.summary: In The Wandering Earth: The Last Full Moon, You Must Get Rid of The Moon
articles.body:
The Sun is going to consume the Earth. Before humanity can fly the planet away, it has to get rid of the Moon.

Author Liu Cixin loves big existential catastrophes. The same fine fellow who casually bent the nature of reality in The Three-Body Problem also wrote a novella of roughly 23,000 Chinese characters that became The Wandering Earth. In turn, this became a 2019 film credited as the moment Chinese cinema proved it could do hard sci-fi at blockbuster scale.

Beyond selling tickets, the film’s success proved the commercial potential of Chinese science-fiction IP and kicked off a wave of new development and creative exploration across the industry.

What’s interesting about The Wandering Earth: The Last Full Moon, the new game from Studio Surgical Scalpels, is that it’s skipping the film entirely and returning to its novella roots. In fact, under the blessing and trust of Cixin, it sees the game as a valid extension of the story, which should please fans.

The studio behind this game is Surgical Scalpels. The team aren’t strangers to space-based games and in fact, it’s their topic du jour. Its last game, Boundary, was a zero-gravity shooter that punched above its weight. This time it’s working with Starry Dome, the studio that holds the licensing rights, after Starry Dome ran an open call back in 2024 (again, officially blessed by Liu Cixin) looking for a developer partner.

According to Frank Mingbo Li, Head of Studio Surgical Scalpels, getting picked was a lengthy courting process.

“The proposal phase lasted 12 months, and we went back and forth for a long time refining that proposal,” Li told me. “This is also how we built trust between the studio and the IP holder.”

The deal came together earlier this year, and development started right after Chinese New Year. There’s already a playable multi-level demo doing the rounds internally.

The novella’s premise is pure Cixin. The sun is going to swell and engulf the Earth within a few centuries, so humanity builds a small army of planetary engines and launches the “Wandering Earth Project”, a 2,500-year mega-plan to fly the entire planet to Proxima Centauri. The first step is to stop the rotation, point the engines the right way, accelerate to escape velocity, coast, then flip everything around and start braking again. This is appropriately called the “Braking Era”. Unfortunately, not everyone is aligned, and The Earth Faction are at odds with The Spaceship Faction. This violent tension is where the action – and gameplay – lie.

The game’s title is a direct reference to Wangri, “the day of the full moon” – the 15th or 16th day of the lunar calendar. In the story, it’s arriving late in the “Braking Era”, when humanity finally has to shove the Moon away from Earth for good.

The full moon usually means reunion in Chinese culture. This story has always been about the opposite: leaving. So the title carries both, the ache of letting go of something familiar and the resolve to keep moving anyway.

You play an engineer sent to the Moon right as that window opens, and things go sideways fast: an assault, a conspiracy and a very old argument reopened.

The novel’s Earth faction and Spaceship faction, two camps who’ve disagreed for 300 years about whether humanity should ride the planet or abandon it for starships, are central to the plot. Don’t expect the studio to spoil how deep that rabbit hole goes. “We can’t spoil any story elements at this stage,” one of the developers told me when I pushed on which other factions might be involved. “If I tell you, I’d have to kill you.”

On the surface (lunar or otherwise), this plays as a third-person shooter first, and the team is oddly insistent about that point. When the obvious Dead Space comparison was brought up, or asked whether Boundary and this game share any DNA beyond genre, the answer was blunt: no.

“We did accumulate a lot of experience, and the setting is shared, but it’s a new IP and it’s not connected,” Li said. “Our motto is to fulfill players’ fantasies for modern shooter games. We want to deliver a grounded, skill-driven shooter. Even with futuristic tools and technology, the gunplay should feel physical and believable, not like an ability-driven sci-fi power fantasy.”

That focus shows up in the toys at your disposal. There’s a backpack-mounted robotic arm that can fling large explosives or haul things no human body should be able to lift, exoskeletons, futuristic sidearms, and eventually space vehicles for getting between the game’s absurdly oversized lunar structures.

None of it, the team insists, is there to replace shooting.

“I wouldn’t say we want to reduce the shooting elements in the game,” Li said. “You can shoot your way from the start to the finish. We’re just adding new ways to interact with the world.”

And in case that wasn’t clear enough, Li repeated it later, looking dead-on, down the metaphorical barrel at me while they said it: “We never compromise the shooting experience.” The point was, suffice to say, driven home.

The aiming system is one of the clearest new ideas here. Instead of a fixed crosshair glued to the center of the screen, Surgical Scalpels is building what it calls a triple-reticle setup, tied to the character model and to lunar gravity rather than to your monitor’s midpoint. In fact, as Li tells me later, the player themselves is the fourth layer of crosshair. Effectively, the player’s physical viewpoint matters above all.

“We want an immersive experience,” Li explained. “The crosshair needs to be tied to the character itself, shown dynamically, at the same time as we show what zero-gravity feels like, how velocity actually works out there.”

It’s the kind of thing that sounds fussy on paper and apparently makes a lot more sense the first time you actually pick up the controller. They’re aware of the risk, too: “We’re aiming for a grounded, high-intensity sci-fi shooter, but we don’t want the controls to feel punishing or needlessly complex.”

We saw looping GIFs of the early targeting system and indeed it does seem like a rethink on how third-person targeting works; in low or zero-gravity environment, you’re factoring in inertia and velocity, and at all times, the team wants you studying your environment, not just staring down the middle of static crosshairs waiting for a target.

Visually, the studio is chasing something it described as grounded rather than fantastical – a “Planetary Engine” or “Lunar Engine” aesthetic, in their words, where “humans could actually build this.” Beyond the trailer, we’ve seen glimpses of concept art, and “dwarfing scale” is what comes to mind. I get the feeling you’ll be made to feel very small in the staggering vastness of space.

As for Liu Cixin’s ongoing involvement, the team seems genuinely pleased with how hands-off he’s been. “He’s very open and tolerant about people being creative with his work,” one of the devs said. “His view is: if your adaptation is a good piece of work, it’s welcome.” The project is being developed under an official license from Starry Dome, the rights holder, which selected the development partner through its own process.

No word yet on official release window or platforms (though they are targeting current consoles and PC), and there are currently no plans for multiplayer. The focus is clearly (and probably rightly) on getting the narrative-driven single player experience just right.

So it’s early days, but, between the moon-shoving stakes, the faction war, and a studio that keeps repeating “we will never undermine the shooting,” and never at the expense of faithful storytelling, I’m hopeful they have the ability to deliver something very special.

IGN was a guest of BiliBili for this preview event.

articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12: First impressions
articles.summary: Reviews News: Apple has launched its next-generation Apple Watch series — Apple Watch Series 12 at the company’s ‘Surprise and Shine ’ event on September 9. With a .
articles.body: Apple has launched its next-generation Apple Watch series — Apple Watch Series 12 at the company’s ‘Surprise and Shine ’ event on September 9. With a starting price tag of Rs 56,900, the Apple Watch Series 12 promises to offer most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable, higher-frequency heart rate and HRV sensing along with the Audio Intelligence features. We spent some time with the Apple Watch Series 12, and here are our initial impressions of Apple’s latest wearable.DesignAt first glance, Series 12 sticks close to the design language Apple Watch has settled into over the past several generations, and that's a deliberate choice rather than a lack of ambition. It comes in the now-familiar 42mm and 46mm sizes, with aluminium models refreshed in dark bronze, black, light gold, and the returning space gray, alongside titanium options in a new radiant gold finish and the existing natural titanium. A striking ceramic version rounds out the lineup in pearl white and night blue, complete with a ceramic pin-and-tuck closure on its matching Sport Bands that pairs nicely with the case.The more meaningful design change is durability rather than aesthetics: aluminum models now use Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple says is 60% tougher than the Ion-X glass on the previous generation. In practice, that's the kind of upgrade you don't notice until the first accidental knock against a doorframe, but it's a welcome move given how often a watch takes small hits over the course of a day. The overall build still feels thin and light on the wrist, in keeping with Apple's continued push to make the watch comfortable enough to wear overnight for sleep tracking without it feeling bulky.Apple hasn't dramatically reworked the display itself this generation, and that's mostly fine. the existing Retina display across aluminum, titanium, and ceramic cases remains sharp, bright, and easy to read at a glance, now protected by the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 cover on aluminum models. Where the display does feel genuinely new is in what it's showing: a new heart rate watch face complication puts real-time heart rate front and center, updating far more frequently than before thanks to the watch's upgraded sensors, and a new Steps complication does the same for step count, both readable in a quick glance without opening an app.The Smart Stack also gets more capable this round, with new contextual widget suggestions — like a parked-car reminder or a birthday nudge for a close contact — surfacing right on the display exactly when they're relevant, alongside a new single-handed tap gesture for selecting individual widgets without needing a second hand free.Features and performanceThis is where Series 12 makes its real case for an upgrade. At the center of it all is Apple's new Health Sensing System, paired with the S11 chip, which Apple says delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable currently on the market — a claim backed by a study spanning more than 1,000 participants comparing it against competing devices.In daily use, the difference shows up in frequency as much as accuracy: the watch now measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, a dramatic jump from previous generations, and tracks heart rate variability up to 24 times more often, split into two distinct metrics — recovery HRV for day-to-day stress signals, and overall HRV for a broader read on cardiovascular health.That denser stream of data feeds directly into the watch's headline new feature: readiness. Each day, Series 12 combines recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score into a single 0-10 score, paired with a plain-language recommendation — Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It. It's a small addition on paper, but in use it functions as a genuinely useful daily gut-check, updating in real time if, say, an intense workout or a shift in vitals changes the picture partway through the day.Battery life sees a solid, if incremental, bump — up to 10 hours during an outdoor workout, a 25% improvement over the previous model, alongside faster charging that now delivers up to 12 hours of extra battery from just 15 minutes on the charger. Step tracking has also been quietly overhauled with new machine learning models, and Apple now claims it as the most accurate step tracking of any smartwatch on the market. Another important additions this time are the new Audio Intelligence features which are said to arrive later this tear. The Live Rewind feature enables you to double-press the Digital Crown and instantly the last b15 seconds of a conversation as text. This is a clever new way to catchup with something you half-missed without asking the other person to repeat. Another interesting feature is Siri Recap which goes further and generate a title and key points from a conversation afterward so that you can revisit it later. Also, Sound Recognition extends existing accessibility features to the wrist, alerting users who are deaf or hard of hearing to sounds like doorbells, alarms, or a crying baby even without an iPhone nearby. Apple has clearly built privacy into the foundation of these features rather than bolting it on afterward — audio is processed in an isolated hardware compartment on the S11 chip and immediately discarded, nothing is stored as a recording, and features like Live Rewind visibly and audibly signal to people nearby when they're active.Layered on top of all this is Siri AI, arriving with watchOS 27, which brings genuine personal context awareness and broader conversational ability to the wrist for the first time, accessible through a new Siri Modular watch face.What we thinkApple Watch Series 12 isn't trying to reinvent what a smartwatch looks like, and that's precisely why it works. The real story here is underneath the display: a genuinely more capable set of health sensors, a readiness score that turns raw vitals into something immediately actionable, and Audio Intelligence features that feel thoughtfully built around privacy. None of it demands you change how you use your watch day to day, but all of it makes the data you're already generating meaningfully more useful. articles.title: Apple Watch Ultra 4: First impressions
articles.summary: Reviews News: Apple Watch Ultra 4 doesn't change what the Ultra line looks like on your wrist, but it changes what it knows about you while it's there. Apple has re.
articles.body: Apple Watch Ultra 4 doesn't change what the Ultra line looks like on your wrist, but it changes what it knows about you while it's there. Apple has refreshed its Watch Ultra lineup with the launch of all new Apple Watch Ultra 4 at the company’s ’Surprise Shine’ event on September 9. Successor to the Apple Watch Ultra 3, the Ultra 4 feature new Health Sensing System, which claims to provide the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable, powerful insights including readiness and longer battery life. We had the chance to spend some time with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, and here are our initial impressions of Apple’s latest rugged wearable.DesignApple Watch Ultra 4 keeps the rugged, unmistakable Ultra silhouette, available in the same natural and black titanium finishes as before. It's a design Apple has clearly settled on as the right one for its most durable watch, and there's no attempt to reinvent it here — the case still feels substantial on the wrist without tipping into cumbersome, and the titanium build continues to feel like it's genuinely built for the outdoors rather than just styled to look like it.The band lineup gets a proper refresh this year. Trail Loop adds dark umber, sand, and burgundy options, while Alpine Loop picks up desert, dark olive, and burgundy. The most interesting material change is on the Ocean Band, now made from a unique translucent silicone available in translucent gray, translucent kelp, and translucent black — a genuinely different look from the solid-colour bands Apple has offered in the past, and one that feels distinctly suited to the Ultra's adventure-sport identity. For Hermès buyers, the collection adds a striking new Grand H titanium band with a built-in extension mechanism that lets it stretch to fit over a wet suit — a small but thoughtful detail for anyone actually using the watch the way Apple markets it.DisplayApple didn't make display technology the headline story with Ultra 4, and that continues a trend from recent Ultra generations — the large, bright, titanium-wrapped display that's made the Ultra legible in direct sunlight and usable with gloves on remains the foundation here. Where the display does become more useful this year is through software: a new heart rate watch face complication surfaces real-time heart rate data at a glance, and a new Steps complication does the same for step count, both readable instantly without opening a separate app. The Smart Stack also becomes more capable, with contextual suggestions — like a parked-car reminder from Maps — surfacing directly on screen, plus a new single-handed tap gesture for selecting individual widgets without needing a free hand.Features and performanceThis is where Apple Watch Ultra 4 makes its real case for an upgrade. At the core is Apple's new Health Sensing System paired with the S11 chip, which Apple says delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable currently available — validated in a study spanning more than 1,000 participants against competing devices. In daily use, the most noticeable change is frequency: heart rate is now measured every five seconds, all day long, and heart rate variability is tracked up to 24 times more often than before, split into recovery HRV for day-to-day stress signals and overall HRV for broader cardiovascular insight.That denser data stream feeds directly into readiness, the watch's headline new feature. Each day, Ultra 4 combines recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score into a single 0-10 score paired with a clear recommendation — Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It — and it updates in real time as new data comes in, whether that's from an intense workout or a shift in daytime vitals. For an audience of athletes and endurance competitors, having that kind of daily gut-check feels like a genuinely practical addition rather than just another number to track.Battery life sees a substantial jump. Everyday use now stretches to up to 50 hours, and Low Power Mode extends that to as much as 84 hours — genuinely multi-day territory for a device this capable. Charging is also faster, with just 15 minutes on the charger adding up to 18 hours of battery back. For outdoor athletes specifically, the new Extended Workout mode delivers up to 25 hours of tracking with full GPS and heart rate data, a 25% jump over the previous model, while the new Max Extended Workout mode stretches that to 45 hours — enough, Apple notes, to track a full 100-mile race while still logging GPS readings every second. Step tracking has also been overhauled with new machine learning models, and Apple now claims it as the most accurate step tracking of any smartwatch, alongside claiming the most accurate on-device GPS in a sports watch.The most forward-looking additions are the new Audio Intelligence features arriving later this year. Live Rewind lets you double-press the Digital Crown to instantly pull up the last 15 seconds of a conversation as text — genuinely useful mid-run or mid-hike when you half-catch something a training partner said. Siri Recap goes further, generating a title and key points from a conversation afterward for later review, and Sound Recognition extends accessibility features to the wrist, alerting users who are deaf or hard of hearing to sounds like sirens or alarms even without an iPhone nearby. Apple has clearly built privacy into these features from the ground up rather than adding it as an afterthought: audio is processed in an isolated hardware compartment on the S11 chip and immediately discarded, nothing is stored as a recording, and features like Live Rewind visibly and audibly signal to people nearby when they're active.Layered on top is Siri AI, arriving with watchOS 27, bringing genuine personal context awareness to the wrist, accessible through a new Siri Modular watch face — a meaningful step up from Siri's previous, more limited capabilities on Apple Watch.What we thinkApple Watch Ultra 4 doesn't ask you to fall in love with a new shape or a flashier screen — it asks you to trust that its sensors, battery, and software have all gotten meaningfully smarter since last year, and on that front, it delivers. The jump to five-second heart rate sensing, the introduction of readiness as an actual daily decision-making tool, and battery life stretching to 45 hours of full GPS tracking for ultra-endurance events are all substantial, practical improvements for the athletes and adventurers this watch is built for. For the complete analysis on the Watch Ultra 4 you will have to wait for our detailed review.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Xbox picks up Kojima’s Physint after PlayStation dropped it
articles.summary: Physint is Xbox’s second upcoming Kojima Productions game, joining OD.
articles.body: Xbox will now publish Physint, an upcoming game from Metal Gear creator Hideo Kojima, after PlayStation decided to cancel it. The unexpected swap came in a flurry of announcements from PlayStation, Xbox, Kojima Productions, and Kojima himself. Sony, which published both of Kojima Productions’ previous Death Stranding games, framed it as a “difficult decision to step away from collaborating with Kojima Productions,” but insisted their “relationship remains strong.” Kojima put things more bluntly on his personal X account, claiming that Sony gave the studio an unexpected cancellation notice in June, and that it has spent the last three months “searching tirelessly” for a new publishing partner. He called Xbox “a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future.” It might have helped that the two companies are already working together, with Xbox lined up to publish the studio’s next game, OD. “Creators have choices about where and how they bring their ideas to life,” said Xbox CEO Asha Sharma in a statement. “We’re honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on Physint. His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox.” Securing a title of Physint’s stature reflects the priorities Sharma laid out in a memo to Xbox staff this summer, promising a focus on “our strongest franchises and biggest new ideas.” The Xbox announcement also notes that the relationship between the two companies will “extend beyond games,” with plans in the works across film and television, though no further details were given. Kojima Productions first announced plans for TV and film projects back in 2021, so far resulting in two upcoming Death Stranding adaptations: an animated spinoff called Mosquito and a live action adaptation from the director of Pig. Kojima calls Physint a “genre-defining action-espionage title,” prompting hopes that it will serve as a spiritual successor to his Metal Gear series, though it’s not expected to launch until at least 2030. OD also has no release date, but should arrive sooner — the horror title was announced in 2022, and a first trailer dropped this time last year.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 System Update 23.0.0 Released — Here Are the Full Patch Notes
articles.summary: Nintendo has released a fresh firmware update, adding VRR support to Switch 2.
articles.body:
Nintendo has released a fresh firmware update for its Switch and Switch 2 consoles, adding VRR support while playing Switch 2 in TV mode.

The ability to toggle on VRR, or variable refresh rate, will of course also rely on your TV supporting this feature. Still, if it does, you'll be able to toggle this on — though bear in mind you'll also just need to activate an update to your Switch 2's dock first. (Finally, Welcome Tour's VRR minigame will be fully playable!)

You'll also now be able to perform a system transfer between two Switch 2 consoles, which will be handy if you're picking up that upcoming Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 special edition console and want to move all your games and settings over.

Nintendo Switch 2: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Console Images

A list of other smaller tweaks lies below for both consoles, though the majority of additions here are for Nintendo's newer machine:

Nintendo Switch 2 - Version 23.0.0 (10th September 2026)

We took the following actions in the “GameChat”:

We’ve added a feature that displays chats you’ve previously participated in, in the list of chats you can join.

We’ve made it possible to join a new chat without selecting any friends.

We’ve added a button to change the screen size in the menu that appears when you press the C button during a chat.

We’ve added a “Settings” option to the “Virtual Game Card” list screen.

You can check the registration status of the device using the virtual game card.

VRR output is now supported in TV mode. When both the software and the TV support it, the video will be output at a refresh rate that matches the game’s processing speed. An update to the Nintendo Switch 2 Dock is required to enable this feature.

Nintendo Switch 2 now supports “complete data transfer” between two Nintendo Switch 2 consoles. You can transfer all your data, including save data and screenshots, from your Switch 2 to your new Switch 2 console.

Made the following changes in “Settings”.

Under “Accessibility” → “Text-to-Speech,” we have added support for text-to-speech in Portuguese (Brazil).

Under “Accessibility” → “Voice-to-Text Conversion for Game Chat,” we’ve added Portuguese (Brazil) to the list of languages ​​for “Text-to-Speech Conversion.”

We’ve made it so that the “Audio” -> “TV Sound” settings are saved for each connected TV.

The item name “Display” → “Dock Output Information” has been changed to “Video Output Information” to allow users to check in detail the video signals that the connected TV can display.

We’ve added a “VRR Settings” option to the “Display” section.

We’ve added a feature to “Mii” that allows you to create a QR code of your Mii and share it with other users.

We’ve added a feature that allows you to instantly play and check the sound when you change the volume under “Sleep” → “Sleep wake-up sound when playing on TV”.

We have added an item to “System” → “Switch Software Operation Mode” → “Toggle Handheld Mode Boost in Quick Settings”. Turning this setting ON will allow you to toggle the Handheld Mode Boost ON/OFF in the Quick Settings menu that appears when you long-press the HOME button.

We’ve added a new option: “System” → “Transfer all to Nintendo Switch 2”.

Even if you cannot transfer the virtual game card from another console when starting the software, you can now temporarily play the software using an online license. If another console is offline and you are unable to transfer the virtual game card, the “Play with Online License” button will appear. Only the person who purchased the software can play it using an online license.

added a feature to play background music in the Mii editing screen. You can switch or stop the background music (BGM) using the “BGM Settings” button in the upper left corner of the screen.

Regarding handheld mode boost, we’ve made it possible to use other controllers even while Joy-Con 2s are attached to the console.

In the “My Page” → “Profile” play record, play time when playing the same software on multiple consoles will now be aggregated. The games you’ve played since the update will be displayed in chronological order.

We have fixed several issues and improved operational stability.

Nintendo Switch 1 - Version 23.0.0 (10th September 2026)

We’ve added a “Settings” option to the “Virtual Game Card” list screen. You can check the registration status of the device using the virtual game card.
